REL-321.name: Hook Called Conditionally, in a Loop or After an Early Return
REL-321.question: Does this component or custom hook call a hook somewhere other than unconditionally at its top level?

javascript: useState, useEffect, useMemo, useContext or a custom useX call inside an if, a ternary, a && expression, a loop, a switch or a try block
a hook call placed after a conditional return, so some renders skip it
a hook called inside a nested function, event handler, callback passed to map, or a class method
every hook call is at the top level of the component or custom hook, before any return
the condition is inside the hook's callback rather than around the hook call
the function named useX is not a React-style hook, or the call is the use API that may be conditional

REL-322.name: Effect, Memo or Callback Dependency List Missing a Value It Reads
REL-322.question: Does a hook callback in this function read a prop, state or local value that its dependency list leaves out, so it keeps using an old value?

javascript: useEffect, useLayoutEffect, useMemo or useCallback whose callback reads props, state or values computed in the component that are absent from the dependency array
an empty dependency array on a callback that reads state or props which change, such as an interval callback reading count
the exhaustive-deps lint rule disabled by a comment above the hook
every reactive value read in the callback is listed, or there is no array and running every render is intended
the omitted values are stable: state setters, dispatch, refs, imports or module constants
the latest value is reached through a ref or a functional state update

distinguish_from.REL-323: a state setter is given a value computed from a stale variable, whatever the dependency list says
distinguish_from.REL-324: the list is complete but the effect changes one of its own entries

REL-323.name: State Update Computed From a Stale Snapshot
REL-323.question: Does this function compute a new state value from a state variable captured earlier, or read state straight after setting it, where the value may be out of date?

javascript: setCount(count + 1) called more than once in one handler, or inside a timer, promise callback or event listener created in an earlier render
setItems([...items, x]) after an await, using the items captured before it
state read on the line after its setter was called, expecting the new value
this.setState({ n: this.state.n + 1 }) in a class component where updates may batch
the functional form is used, such as setCount(c => c + 1) or setState(prev => ...)
the new value does not depend on the previous state
a reducer or ref holds the value

distinguish_from.REL-309: state is changed in place rather than computed from an old copy

REL-324.name: Effect or Render Body That Updates the State It Depends On
REL-324.question: Does this component set state during render, or in an effect that runs again because of that same update, so it can re-render without end?

javascript: a state setter called directly in the component body, outside any handler or effect and with no guarding condition
useEffect with no dependency array that sets state every time it runs
an effect that sets a state variable listed in its own dependencies, or sets state to a new object or array that a dependency is derived from
onClick={setOpen(true)} or onClick={handle()} that updates state while rendering
the update is guarded so it stops, such as comparing with the previous value before setting
the setter runs in an event handler, or in an effect whose dependencies the update does not change
the value is derived during render or with useMemo instead of being stored in state

distinguish_from.REL-345: a function is called at once where a callback was expected, with no state update that re-triggers rendering

REL-325.name: Async Result Applied After Unmount or After a Newer Request Started
REL-325.question: Does an effect or handler in this function start an asynchronous request and apply its result without checking that it is still the latest request for a mounted component?

javascript: useEffect that fetches using a prop or state value and calls a state setter in then or after await, with no cleanup that cancels or ignores the response
a search or autocomplete handler that sets results from each response, so a slow early response overwrites a later one
a state setter called after an await in a component that may have unmounted, with no AbortController or ignore flag
the effect's cleanup aborts the request or sets a flag checked before the state is set
a data library such as React Query, SWR or a router loader owns the request
the request does not depend on changing input and runs once

distinguish_from.REL-300: a listener, timer or subscription is left registered, rather than a response applied late
distinguish_from.REL-312: the shared state is not component state set from a request

REL-326.name: List Items Rendered With Missing, Index or Unstable Keys
REL-326.question: Does this function render a list of elements whose keys are missing, taken from the array index, or regenerated on each render, although the list can reorder, grow or shrink?

javascript: items.map(item => <Row ... />) with no key prop on the returned element
key={index} or key={i} on a list that is sorted, filtered, prepended to or has items removed, especially when rows hold inputs or local state
key={Math.random()}, key={uuid()} or key={Date.now()} computed during render
the key is a stable identifier from the data, such as item.id
the list is static and never reordered, so an index key is harmless
the key is on a fragment or element that is not part of a list

REL-327.name: Numeric or Empty-String Condition Rendered by && in JSX
REL-327.question: Does this function use value && <Element /> in JSX where the value can be 0, NaN or an empty string, so that value itself is rendered or the element is wrongly hidden?

javascript: {count && <Badge />}, {items.length && <List />} or {total && ...}, which renders 0 when the number is zero

{text &&

...

} in React Native, where an empty string outside a Text element is an error
the left side is a boolean, such as count > 0, !!value, Boolean(value) or a comparison
a ternary with an explicit null branch is used
the value is an object, array or boolean that can never be 0 or an empty string

distinguish_from.REL-230: the truthiness test is not the left side of && in rendered markup
